breaking_news.headline: Google launches Project Suncatcher, a step towards AI data centers in space
breaking_news.summary: The fridge-size satellite with AI chips on board is part of Project Suncatcher, the company's moonshot effort to put AI data centers in space and harness solar energy.

breaking_news.headline: Breweries adapt as tastes in beer change
breaking_news.summary: The craft beer market is saturated and tastes are changing. Brewers are coming with innovative ways to attract customers.

breaking_news.headline: The U.S. Senate is up for grabs. Can this Ohio Democrat win back working class votes?
breaking_news.summary: After 32 years in Congress, Ohio's Sherrod Brown lost his Senate seat in 2024 as many working class voters turned out for Trump. Now Brown is counting on union voters to send him back to Washington.

breaking_news.headline: San Francisco's car crime has plunged. How much credit does Flock deserve?
breaking_news.summary: San Francisco leaders say AI-powered cameras helped drive a dramatic decline in car crime. We examine the evidence — and whether the city can keep its high-tech dragnet without sacrificing civil liberties.

breaking_news.headline: Why is diesel more expensive than regular gas?
breaking_news.summary: Diesel hasn't always been more expensive than other gasoline. Then in 2004, a switch happened due to air quality standards, demand, and taxes. In this week's Indicator newsletter, we dig into diesel prices, what kind of fun people are buyin

breaking_news.headline: The U.S. added only 29,000 jobs in September as job market lacks spark
breaking_news.summary: U.S. employers added 29,000 jobs in September as the unemployment rate inched up to 4.2%. Job gains for July and August were revised down by a total of 60,000 jobs, extending a lackluster run for the job market.

breaking_news.headline: Pro-Trump Influencer Benny Johnson is being sued for defamation by ICE protesters
breaking_news.summary: The lawsuit says the prominent conservative podcaster falsely claimed the protesters were assaulting ICE officers during demonstrations at an ICE facility in Illinois last year.

breaking_news.headline: Economist Betsey Stevenson breaks down the gender gap in recent hiring reports
breaking_news.summary: The U.S. economy added fewer jobs than expected last month and unemployment ticked up to 4.2%. NPR's Scott Simon talks to Betsey Stevenson, an economist at the University of Michigan.

breaking_news.headline: Why has Brazil accused the US of election interference?
breaking_news.summary: The Latin American country will vote for its next president, as Lula da Silva and Bolsonaro clash over sovereignty, security and ties with Washington.

breaking_news.headline: Debris found from plane that went missing off US coast
breaking_news.summary: The aircraft lost communication with flight controllers after significantly dropping in altitude, according to flight data.

breaking_news.headline: 'Anger in the streets': Tens of thousands protest in Spain over housing crisis
breaking_news.summary: More than 50 protests took place on Saturday after the government failed to get emergency legislation through parliament.

breaking_news.headline: Russia hits second major bridge in Ukraine's capital Kyiv
breaking_news.summary: The strike on the Pivnichnyi (Northern) Bridge comes after repeat attacks on another major bridge in Ukraine's capital.

breaking_news.headline: Flydubai co-pilot attacked captain with axe, UAE official says
breaking_news.summary: The man accused of trying to take over the Israel-bound jet is named as Hamam al-Hammami by several media outlets.

breaking_news.headline: Cornell president says university 'must do better' after frat house rape allegations
breaking_news.summary: Michael Kotlikoff described the allegations of a woman who says she was drugged and gang raped as "deeply disturbing".

breaking_news.headline: Tennessee prison chief to resign after Christa Pike's failed execution
breaking_news.summary: Pike's lawyers said the failure "goes far beyond any one person". Pike is in critical condition after surviving two lethal injections.

breaking_news.headline: No more cereal at the end of the aisle? New rules in Scotland's supermarkets
breaking_news.summary: Restrictions are being put on products with high sugar, fat and salt content, but the meal deal lives on.

breaking_news.headline: What's gone wrong at Nike? How the world's sportswear giant lost its mojo
breaking_news.summary: Several self-inflicted mistakes have cost the biggest sportswear brand on the planet in recent years.

breaking_news.headline: The wealthy Cuban Americans ready and waiting for Havana to fall
breaking_news.summary: Cuban exiles in Florida are increasingly hopeful that regime change in Cuba is now on the horizon.

breaking_news.headline: 'It could cost me £10k but I need the money now': Why Gen Z are opting out of pensions
breaking_news.summary: A growing number of people are opting out of these schemes due to cost-of-living pressures.

breaking_news.headline: US jobs market sees sharp slowdown ahead of midterm elections
breaking_news.summary: Unemployment rose slightly as American employers paused hiring with midterm elections just a month away.
